_note: EDITORIAL data. The measured half lives in hearing_rates.json and is regenerated by the Legislative Research Tool — never hand-edit rates into this file. Characters are FICTIONAL; the committees, codes, route and deadlines are real. SCOPE: the two MONEY committees only — House Finance and Senate Ways and Means. Every bill with a dollar figure goes through both, they take more referrals than any other committee (876 and 936 in 2026) and they hand back the two lowest hearing rates, so they are where the module's argument lives. Subject-matter committees are deliberately out of scope; if they come back, restore the `singleReferral` roll with them. `championed` is the one place a measured rate is deliberately adjusted: the base covers EVERY measure referred, including the thousands nobody carries, and the player's bills have their introducer working them every week.

dilution._note: Distinct failure modes: low influence still kills a bill outright (never heard, unchanged). Low SUPPORT no longer just nudges the same hearing roll — the moment a bill clears a chair gate, if its support is under floor, it comes out smaller. Multiplicative and stacks across the two money-committee gates (a chronically unpopular bill can limp out of both already thin), floored so dilution alone never zeroes a bill — killing it stays the job of never-heard/voted-down/conference.

familyTilt._note: EDITORIAL, not measured — same standard as `championed` above: named, small, a judgment call about who a tax family's natural base is, not survey data. Seeds a bill's OWN support/influence away from the campaign's global numbers at introduction: wealth taxes poll well and lack institutional access; GET is the reverse (broad, visible, unpopular — but the lever leadership reaches for precisely because it avoids concentrated opposition); credits and tourism/admin sit closest to the measured hearing-rate story (session's easiest gates). Deltas are added to S.metrics.support/influence at seed time, then clamped 0-100 — they do not touch the measured base rate in baseRate(), which stays untouched by design.

causes.never heard: The chair never put it on a hearing calendar. No vote was taken, and no record exists of it dying.
causes.voted down: It got a vote and lost.
causes.died in conference: The two chambers could not agree on a final version before the deadline.
causes.ran out of clock: The deadline passed while it was still waiting.
